edges.relation: Carroll-Ortega-Cerda used Fedorov's Polya-Chebotarev solution for 4 symmetric points to determine the optimal arc placement in their harmonically symmetric slit domain. The arc endpoints are exactly the points in the Polya-Chebotarev problem.
Conformal welding was the technique used to prove existence of harmonically symmetric domains. The welding homeomorphism encodes the harmonic symmetry condition.

The logarithmic capacity of the Polya-Chebotarev continuum determines the conformal radius, which in turn bounds the hyperbolic metric density of the complementary domain. Minimizing capacity maximizes the conformal radius and affects hyperbolic density.
SC mapping can approximate conformal maps to slit domains (after polygonal approximation of arcs). Interval arithmetic provides rigorous error bounds on the resulting B_u estimate.
SC mappings provide training data and validation for neural conformal map approximations. The neural network can interpolate between SC solutions for different domain configurations.
The expected Brownian exit time equals the integral of the torsion function, which is spectrally determined. The first eigenvalue lambda_1 bounds the exit time from above: E_z[tau] <= 1/lambda_1.
The hyperbolic metric sigma controls the Green's function, which is the kernel for the expected exit time. Banuelos-Carroll used sigma >= 1/(2R) to derive lifetime bounds.
The hyperbolic metric density of the hexagonal lattice complement is computed via Weierstrass elliptic functions. Eremenko studied this connection to bound the Landau constant.
Baernstein-Vinson's local minimality proof uses variational methods: they compute the second variation of B_f at the Ahlfors-Grunsky function within the lattice covering class.
Level set methods are well-established for spectral eigenvalue optimization. The same computational framework can optimize the spectral quantities related to B_u.

Level set methods can discover the slit structure of extremal domains by evolving from simple initial shapes. If the optimizer converges to slit domains, this validates the harmonic symmetry approach.
Schiffer variations deform the conformal map within the schlicht class. Quasiconformal deformations generalize this to maps with bounded dilatation, providing a larger class of test perturbations.
Conformal welding produces conformal maps, while quasiconformal deformations relax the conformality requirement. The Beltrami coefficient measures the failure of the welding to be conformal.
The neural surrogate replaces the expensive conformal map computation in the level set inner loop, enabling faster shape optimization iterations.
Torsion rigidity P(D) = 2 * int u = E_0[tau_D] * |D|^{-1} * int 1 connects directly to expected Brownian lifetime. The spectral gap lambda_1 controls the exponential decay of the exit time tail.

Quasiconformal deformations of the hexagonal lattice covering provide a larger class of perturbations than Baernstein-Vinson considered. Testing whether local minimality persists under qc deformations would strengthen the Ahlfors-Grunsky conjecture.
The Polya-Chebotarev extremal continuum can be found via a level-set evolution that minimizes capacity. Both problems are shape optimization with a potential-theoretic objective.

bridge_chains.name: Probabilistic → Spectral → Geometric
bridge_chains.description: Start from Brownian motion exit times (probability), connect to eigenvalue bounds (spectral theory), then to hyperbolic metric density (differential geometry), ending at lattice structure (discrete geometry). Each step tightens the relationship between probabilistic quantities and the Bloch constant.

bridge_chains.name: Computational → Verified → Rigorous
bridge_chains.description: Start with fast but approximate neural computation (ML), feed candidates into interval-arithmetic SC verification (numerical analysis), apply to specific domain classes (complex analysis), grounded in capacity theory (potential theory). This chain converts heuristic exploration into rigorous bounds.

bridge_chains.name: Variational → Topological → Optimization
bridge_chains.description: Start from classical Schiffer variations (calculus of variations), generalize to quasiconformal deformations (Teichmuller theory), use conformal welding to construct domains (topology), and optimize domain shapes via level sets (computational optimization). This chain systematically enlarges the search space for extremal domains.

bridge_chains.name: Lattice → Capacity → Slits → Bounds
bridge_chains.description: Start from the conjectured hexagonal lattice extremal (discrete geometry), use capacity optimization to determine arc placement (potential theory), construct harmonically symmetric slit domains (complex analysis), and verify bounds rigorously (numerical analysis). This is the pipeline that led to the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound.
